p2:c.evidence: reports/task6-summary-evidence/academic/dated-controller-comparison/0928.json question p2, subpart c; frozen dated-group1/results.json; root-adjudication.json. The normal equation and inverse formula agree only for full column rank. Current verify/pitfall disclose four distinct inputs as sufficient and a generalized inverse/nonuniqueness alternative when rank deficient. Marginal Uniform draws alone do not prove rank.
p2:c.conclusion: Full-rank formula: theta_ML=(Phi^T Phi)^(-1)Phi^T y. In general use the stated pseudoinverse family.
derivation: With independent common Gaussian observation variance sigma^2=0.04, negative log likelihood equals ||y-Phi theta||^2/(2sigma^2)+constant.
Its gradient is Phi^T(Phi theta-y)/sigma^2. Setting it to zero yields Phi^T Phi theta=Phi^T y.
If Phi has column rank 4, Phi^T Phi is invertible and theta_ML=(Phi^T Phi)^(-1)Phi^T y. If rank deficient, all least-squares minimizers are Phi^+y+(I_4-Phi^+Phi)w for arbitrary w in R^4.
checks: Phi^T Phi is 4x4 and Phi^T y is 4x1.
At least four distinct x values suffice for the cubic Vandermonde matrix to have rank 4.
No actual input values or labels are provided, so a numerical theta is not identifiable.
unresolved_in_frozen: Full column rank is not stated. Marginal x_n~Uniform[-5,5] alone does not guarantee distinct inputs without a sampling-dependence assumption; the inverse formula is conditional on rank 4. The usual independent continuous draws have full rank with probability 1.
p2:c.comparison_condition: The normal equation and inverse formula agree only for full column rank. Current verify/pitfall disclose four distinct inputs as sufficient and a generalized inverse/nonuniqueness alternative when rank deficient. Marginal Uniform draws alone do not prove rank.

p3:a.evidence: reports/task6-summary-evidence/academic/dated-controller-comparison/0928.json question p3, subpart a; frozen dated-group1/results.json; root-adjudication.json. Noise variance 0.2^2=1/25 divided by the current prior variance 1/4 gives 4/25=0.16, with the identity matching feature dimension.
derivation: Observation variance sigma^2=0.2^2=0.04=1/25. Prior covariance b^2 I=(1/4)I, so b^2=1/4.
Divide variance by variance: (1/25)/(1/4)=4/25.
checks: b=1/2 if taken as a positive standard deviation; using b^2=1/4 avoids confusing variance with standard deviation.
The ridge addition is (4/25)I_K, matching the KxK Gram matrix.
Prior negative log penalty is ||theta||^2/(2b^2); multiplying the MAP normal equation by sigma^2 yields the displayed coefficient.

p3:b.evidence: reports/task6-summary-evidence/academic/dated-controller-comparison/0928.json question p3, subpart b; frozen dated-group1/results.json; root-adjudication.json. Degree 8 is an example-specific tendency, not a universal theorem: y=0 makes both estimates zero. Current solve/verify/pitfall disclose this. Actual MML Figure9.7 corroborates its historical 6/8-degree illustration, with prior I rather than the current adapted I/4.
p3:b.conclusion: Expected qualitative choice: degree 8 often shows more regularization; no unconditional ordering can be deduced from the supplied data.
derivation: For Gram eigenvalue d>=0, ridge changes the unregularized eigen-direction coefficient by the shrinkage factor d/(d+lambda), lambda=4/25; smaller d is more strongly changed.

An eighth-degree polynomial has nine parameters; a sixth-degree polynomial has seven. Extra high-power directions often have weak data constraints, instability, or a large coefficient norm, so regularization commonly becomes more apparent at degree 8.
However the actual spectrum and Phi^T y depend on input values and labels; degree alone does not force a strictly larger effect. For instance, y=0 gives identical zero estimates for both degrees.
checks: For any nonzero v, v^T(Phi^T Phi+lambda I)v=||Phi v||^2+lambda||v||^2>0, so the MAP system is invertible for lambda=0.16.
The prior shrinks coefficients in the supplied monomial coordinate system; no rescaling or coefficient exemption is assumed.
unresolved_in_frozen: No realized design, labels, or quantitative definition of regularization effect is supplied, so a definitive comparison between degree 6 and degree 8 is unresolved.
p3:b.comparison_condition: Degree 8 is an example-specific tendency, not a universal theorem: y=0 makes both estimates zero. Current solve/verify/pitfall disclose this. Actual MML Figure9.7 corroborates its historical 6/8-degree illustration, with prior I rather than the current adapted I/4.

p4:main.comparison_condition: Product/chain rules give 4sin(x^3)/x+3x^2 ln(x^4)cos(x^3), for x≠0. Current pitfall preserves 4ln|x| on the full real domain.

p6:a.evidence: reports/task6-summary-evidence/academic/dated-controller-comparison/0928.json question p6, subpart a; frozen dated-group1/results.json; root-adjudication.json. The scalar chain 1x1 times 1xD gives 2x^T/(1+x^Tx); denominator is positive for all real x.
p6:a.conclusion: df/dx=2x^T/(1+x^T x), size 1xD; equivalently column gradient is 2x/(1+x^T x).
derivation: Use the Jacobian convention J_ij=partial output_i/partial input_j, so scalar derivatives with respect to a vector are rows.
df/dz=1/(1+z), size 1x1; dz/dx=2x^T, size 1xD.
Multiply in chain order: df/dx=(1/(1+x^T x))*2x^T.
checks: x^T x>=0 implies 1+z>=1, so the logarithm domain is valid for every real x.
(1x1)(1xD) gives 1xD; no transpose ambiguity after fixing the convention.
p6:a.comparison_condition: The scalar chain 1x1 times 1xD gives 2x^T/(1+x^Tx); denominator is positive for all real x.

p6:b.evidence: reports/task6-summary-evidence/academic/dated-controller-comparison/0928.json question p6, subpart b; frozen dated-group1/results.json; root-adjudication.json. Component derivative cos(z_i)A_ij agrees with diag(cos z)A, an ExD Jacobian with factors ExE and ExD.
derivation: For componentwise sin, partial f_i/partial z_j=delta_ij cos(z_i), so df/dz=diag(cos(z)), size ExE.
For z=Ax+b, dz/dx=A, size ExD. Chain rule yields df/dx=diag(cos(Ax+b))A.
checks: (ExE)(ExD) gives ExD.
Component (i,j) is cos((Ax+b)_i) A_ij; b contributes no derivative with respect to x.
p6:b.comparison_condition: Component derivative cos(z_i)A_ij agrees with diag(cos z)A, an ExD Jacobian with factors ExE and ExD.

p7:main.evidence: reports/task6-summary-evidence/academic/dated-controller-comparison/0928.json question p7, subpart main; frozen dated-group1/results.json; root-adjudication.json. Elementwise tanh derivative is a diagonal MxM matrix, multiplied on the left of the MxN A; the MxN result and b derivative zero agree.
p7:main.conclusion: df/dx=diag(1-tanh^2 z) A, size MxN, where z=Ax+b.
derivation: For elementwise tanh, d f_i/d z_j=delta_ij(1-tanh^2 z_i). Thus df/dz=diag(1-tanh^2 z), MxM.
dz/dx=A, MxN. Chain rule df/dx=(df/dz)(dz/dx)=diag(1-tanh^2(Ax+b))A.
checks: Jacobian convention: output coordinates index rows; input coordinates index columns.
(MxM)(MxN)=MxN; b is Mx1 and has zero derivative with respect to x.
Every real z_i is valid; 0<1-tanh^2 z_i<=1 for finite z_i.
p7:main.comparison_condition: Elementwise tanh derivative is a diagonal MxM matrix, multiplied on the left of the MxN A; the MxN result and b derivative zero agree.

p8:main.evidence: reports/task6-summary-evidence/academic/dated-controller-comparison/0928.json question p8, subpart main; frozen dated-group1/results.json; root-adjudication.json. The two negative chain factors cancel, giving exp(-x)/(1+exp(-x))^2=f(1-f); at x=0 the derivative is 1/4.
derivation: Write f=(1+exp(-x))^(-1). Chain rule gives f prime=-(1+exp(-x))^(-2)*(-exp(-x))=exp(-x)/(1+exp(-x))^2.
Also 1-f=exp(-x)/(1+exp(-x)); multiplying by f gives the same derivative.
checks: Denominator positive for all real x; derivative positive and at most 1/4 since t(1-t)<=1/4 for 0<t<1.
Own symbolic derivative minus f(1-f) simplifies exactly to zero.
p8:main.comparison_condition: The two negative chain factors cancel, giving exp(-x)/(1+exp(-x))^2=f(1-f); at x=0 the derivative is 1/4.
